abstract:
Gastric cancer is a heterogeneous disease shaped by the co-evolution of malignant epithelial programs, stromal remodeling, and immune contexture. Transfer RNA (tRNA) regulation sits at a strategic junction in this biology: it governs translational capacity and selectivity while generating tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs) and tRNA halves (tiRNAs)-a family of regulatory small RNAs detectable in both tissue and blood.
We asked whether the coordinated machinery responsible for tRNA transcription, maturation, modification, charging, and cleavage defines biologically meaningful gastric cancer ecosystem states, and whether a corresponding circulating small-RNA phenotype can be detected across independent cohorts of chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG), early gastric cancer (EGC), and gastric cancer (GC).
We integrated transcriptomic, genomic, proteomic, and tissue small-RNA data across complementary gastric cancer series and localized the program in single-cell expression maps. The clinical arm comprised independent serum samples from CAG, EGC, and GC participants.
A 70-gene tRNA-regulatory program resolved three ecosystem states (TRES-1, TRES-2, and TRES-3). TRES-3 exhibited high tRNA-regulatory activity coupled with proliferative and DNA-repair protein expression, whereas TRES-1 was enriched for receptor-signaling and cell-cycle-restraint proteins. These states also differed in copy-number alterations and non-synonymous variant burden at the program level. Direct tissue small-RNA profiling revealed a marked expansion of tRF output and repertoire breadth in TRES-2 and TRES-3, with state-specific tRF classes, parent-tRNA modules, and exact sequences. A shared set of 446 exact tRF sequences connected the tissue and serum catalogues. In an independent gastric cancer series, the three-state architecture aligned with ACRG molecular subtypes, RNA cargo selection, extracellular vesicle release, and stress-response programs. Single-cell mapping placed tRNA-regulatory activity across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments. In our serum cohort, the 14-30-nt fraction declined from 47.4% in CAG to 37.8% in EGC and 33.6% in GC, while the 31-40-nt fraction rose from 52.6% to 62.2% and 66.4% (absolute Spearman rho = 0.791; BH-adjusted P = 0.0112; exact-permutation P = 0.0214).
tRNA regulation defines gastric cancer ecosystem states with distinct genomic, proteomic, and tissue small-RNA correlates. In our serum cohort, the reciprocal shift in circulating tRF/tiRNA length composition-a decline in the 14-30-nt fraction and a rise in the 31-40-nt fraction-parallels the transition from CAG to EGC to GC. These findings establish a testable molecular framework for paired tissue-serum validation and position circulating tRF/tiRNA architecture as a candidate readout of gastric cancer ecosystem biology.

title: tRNA regulatory ecosystem states shape tissue and circulating small-RNA landscapes in gastric cancer.
